newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES MIXED IN LIQUID MARKET.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES MIXED IN LIQUID MARKET.

text.p: Short-term trading rates on Zimbabwe's money market were quoted mixed on Thursday in continued liquidity though dealers expected the market to be short as banks made their statutory payments to government.
"Nothing much is happening on the market so far but banks are making their statutory payments and since there are no maturities today the market might be a little bit short," a dealer said.
Discount houses were on Thursday taking up 91-day central bank bills at 19.60 percent and selling them back into the market at the same rate.
The buying rate for 30-, 60- and 90-day NCDs slipped to 24 percent from 25.50 percent but they were selling firmer at 23 percent from 22 percent.
Bankers acceptance bills were at 21 and 20.50 percent, from 21.50 and 20.50 percent while call money added one percentage point to 23 percent.
The central Reserve Bank indicated an opening surplus figure in the market of Z$157 million, down from Z$523 million the previous day.
